documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Rooming: vitals done, seated 5 min before BP. Meds verified verbally. Still smoking. No falls since last visit.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u CAD, HTN, COPD, PAD.

Winter was long. More short of breath this winter than last - gets winded walking from the truck to the store in the cold. Cough most mornings, white. No fever, no hemoptysis. No chest pain. Calves cramp at two blocks, same.
Using olodaterol most mornings.
Smoking 1 ppd.

Vitals: BP 155/90, HR 70, SpO2 94% RA, wt 92.9 kg.
Exam: Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs: diminished throughout, prolonged expiration, end-expiratory wheeze. Ext no edema. Feet intact.

A/P
1. HTN - 155/90 today. Continue lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succ 50.
2. CAD s/p MI - no angina. Continue ASA, statin, BB, ACEi.
3. COPD - more dyspnea this winter. Continue olodaterol. Will see how he does into spring.
4. PAD - stable claudication. Walking.
5. Tobacco - counseled. Declines.

RTC 2-3 mo.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed for f/u. Med rec complete. Pt reports no ED visits or hospital stays since last visit. Tobacco use: yes, daily.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: breathing worse.

He says the breathing has been sliding for a few years and the spring didn't bring it back the way it usually does. Now stops halfway up his stairs. Chronic cough, white sputum, no change in color. No fever, chills, weight loss, chest pain or leg swelling. No hemoptysis.
Has never had formal breathing tests that he knows of - the COPD diagnosis came from his old doctor.
Smoking 1 ppd.

Vitals: BP 148/97, HR 70, SpO2 91% RA, T 37.0.
Exam: barrel-chested. Breath sounds diminished, prolonged expiration, occasional wheeze. No crackles. Heart regular. No peripheral edema.

A/P
1. COPD with progressive dyspnea - no PFTs on file ever. Referral to pulmonology for full PFTs and recommendations. Continue olodaterol daily meanwhile.
2. HTN - 148/97. Continue current meds.
3. Tobacco - he connects the breathing to the cigarettes. Still not ready to set a date.
4. CAD/PAD - stable.

RTC after pulm.

documents.title: Pulmonology referral
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pulmonology scheduled pt for consult + full PFTs 7/13. Pt aware; told to hold olodaterol the morning of testing per their instructions sheet, mailed.

reports.text:
PULMONARY FUNCTION LABORATORY - COMPLETE PFTs (spirometry, lung volumes)
Technically acceptable and reproducible efforts.
Spirometry: FVC decreased. FEV1 severely decreased. FEV1/FVC ratio decreased.
Lung volumes: TLC increased. FRC increased. RV increased.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive ventilatory defect with severely reduced FEV1, hyperinflation and air trapping. Consistent with COPD.

documents.title: Pulmonology Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY CONSULTATION
Visit date: 07/13/2022

Referred by primary care for progressive dyspnea.

HPI: 68-year-old man with COPD treated with olodaterol, coronary disease after MI with PCI, and PAD. Shortness of breath has progressed over the past few years. He has a chronic cough productive of white sputum. He denies chest pain, fever and weight loss. Current smoker, 45 pack-years per our intake.

Exam: SpO2 92% on room air. Barrel-chested. Diminished breath sounds with a prolonged expiratory phase and an occasional wheeze.

PFTs today: obstruction with a decreased FVC, severely decreased FEV1 and a reduced FEV1/FVC ratio. TLC, FRC and RV are all increased, consistent with hyperinflation and air trapping.

Impression: COPD, first formal physiologic confirmation; severe airflow obstruction with hyperinflation.

Plan: The key intervention is stopping smoking, which we discussed. Return to pulmonology clinic in about a year, sooner if worse.

orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Vitals obtained. Med list reviewed, pharmacy confirmed (mail-order). Current smoker. Pt asked for printed after-visit summary.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV subsequent.

Pulmonology letter from 7/13 reviewed: first full PFTs - severe obstruction, FEV1 severely reduced, hyperinflation/air trapping. Their plan: smoking cessation, see him in a year. He's still on olodaterol alone.
Feels about the same as the spring. Stops on stairs. No chest pain.

HRA: independent. No falls. PHQ-2 1 ('tired of being out of breath'). Alcohol 1-2/wk.
Tobacco: 1 ppd, ~47 pk-yr.

Vitals: BP 143/94, HR 63, SpO2 92%.
Exam: barrel chest, diminished BS, prolonged exp. Heart RRR. Abd soft, pulsatile mass. Pedal pulses diminished.

Prevention:
- LDCT annual - ordered.
- FIT kit given.
- Due: PCV20 (PPSV23 2019), Shingrix, COVID bivalent, flu - October nurse visit, he agreed to all of it in one trip.

A/P
1. COPD, severe obstruction on PFTs - continue olodaterol per pulm.
2. HTN - 143/94. Continue lisinopril/HCTZ/metoprolol.
3. CAD/HLD - labs today.
4. AAA - vascular surgery surveillance; last 4.3 cm 7/2021.
5. Tobacco - counseled. Declines.

RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called with AWV labs per PCP. Kidney function, potassium and blood count normal (creatinine 1.0). LDL 75 on atorvastatin, no change. Pt aware. Reminded about FIT kit.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING - ANNUAL
Comparison: 08/24/2021, 08/11/2020.
Lungs: Upper lobe predominant centrilobular emphysema. 4 mm right upper lobe solid nodule, stable over two years. No new or growing nodule.
Pleura and mediastinum: Unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 2, benign. Emphysema. Continue annual LDCT.

documents.title: Lung CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lyle - yearly lung CT is benign again (Lung-RADS 2). The tiny nodule hasn't changed in two years. The emphysema is there as before. Next scan in a year. Still haven't seen the stool kit come back - please mail it in.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Four vaccines per PCP order, pt preferred one trip:
- High-dose flu, R deltoid
- PCV20, R deltoid (lower site, 1 inch apart)
- Pfizer bivalent COVID booster, L deltoid
- Shingrix dose 1, L deltoid (lower site)
VIS/fact sheets given. Warned about sore arms and feeling run down for a day or two with Shingrix. Observed 15 min, fine. Shingrix #2 booked for January.
